app.run: HeidelBridge is ESP32 firmware; nothing of it runs on this Mac. The one device runs at the owner's Heidelberg wallbox and is reachable on the LAN at http://heidelbridge. It is in production: Home Assistant controls the wallbox through it over MQTT. Build with `pio run -e esp32` (about a minute the first time; the image lands in `.pio/build/esp32/firmware.bin`). After any change under `data/` (HTML, JS, CSS of the web interface) run `./build-resources.sh` first and commit the regenerated `data/headers/*.h`, otherwise the firmware still serves the old files. `pio run -e dummy` builds a variant with a simulated wallbox (for a spare ESP32 on USB; none is attached), and `pio test -e native` runs the host-side unit tests. Never flash, reboot or change settings on the device without the owner's explicit OK on the card (ask first). Once they agree, `./tools/ota_upload.sh` uploads the built image over the air (WiFi/MQTT settings stay, charging continues across the reboot) and waits until `http://heidelbridge/api/version` answers with the new version. Without that OK, only look: open http://heidelbridge for the configuration page (password fields are masked; do not edit the energy counter and do not press 'Apply and restart') and http://heidelbridge/api/version for the running version and build date; http://heidelbridge/update is the OTA page (do not upload from it). For a demo of a change to the web interface before it is flashed, serve `data/` locally (`python3 -m http.server 0 --directory data` in the background picks a free port and prints it; stop it by its PID afterwards): the page renders, but its form stays empty since the device's API is not there. No login is needed. Nothing else runs locally, so there is nothing to stop.
